headline: Record profits at Ratings and Indices as Mobility spins off
summary_short: GAAP revenue rose 10% y/y to $4,146M and diluted EPS rose 18% to $4.12, with record segment profit at Ratings (+28%) and Indices (+21%) driving the gain even as the company completed the Mobility Global spin-off on July 1, 2026.
summary_long: Revenue grew 10% y/y to $4.146B; GAAP operating profit rose 17% to $1.812B on record results at Ratings (op. profit +28%) and Indices (+21%), driven by ratings issuance strength and index asset-linked/subscription growth, while Market Intelligence and Energy grew more modestly. The company completed the Mobility Global spin-off on July 1, 2026; pro forma continuing-operations revenue was $3.678B (+11% y/y) with adjusted diluted EPS of $4.83 (+23%). Quarterly buybacks were $500M ($1.5B YTD); the board declared a $0.97/share dividend. Cash rose to $4.141B after a $2.0B senior-notes issuance. FY2026 guidance (ex-Mobility): revenue growth 5.9%-7.9%, GAAP diluted EPS $16.35-$16.60.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited record results in two of our benchmark businesses — Ratings and Indices; segment data show Ratings +17% on issuance strength and Indices +20% on asset-linked/subscription growth, while Market Intelligence (+6%) and Energy (+2%) grew more modestly.
Release states margin improvement on both a GAAP and adjusted basis was driven primarily by growth and margin expansion in the Ratings, Indices, and Market Intelligence divisions.
On a pro forma basis, diluted EPS growth of 26% reflects a 22% rise in net income plus a 3% reduction in diluted shares outstanding from ongoing buybacks.

CEO Martina Cheung highlighted record results at Ratings and Indices, successful completion of the Mobility Global spin-off on July 1, and continued rapid adoption of AI solutions across the business.
